To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the stock of international indebtedness, the real exchange, and the consumption level are all determined by the initial conditions of the economy; and (b) the stock of debt, the real, and consumption all adjust to a new steady state in response to a shock to the economy.

the stock of debt is stable and that the real exchange rate and consumption are not stable under a lending arrangement linking interest rates to the trade balance, but that the stock of international borrowing is stable and that real exchange rates and consumption are not necessarily unstable under a lending arrangement that links interest rates to the outstanding stock.

(i) the interest rates on international lending are likely to have a large impact on the adjustment path of the economy, and (ii) the interest rates should be linked to the outstanding stock rather than the current account deficit.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the debt overhang problem of developing countries can be resolved by linking the interest rates on lending and borrowing to the performance on the trade account.
the question of whether a country that borrows from abroad to finance a current-account deficit can sustain a stable macroeconomic equilibrium.
the question of the stability of the international debt stock in a small open economy in the context of a model of intertemporal optimization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more a lending arrangement links interest rates to the stock of debt, the less likely it is to be unstable.
the best way to ensure a smooth adjustment path for a small open country is to avoid lending arrangements that link interest rates to measures of creditworthness.
the arrangements linking lending interest rates to performance of the trade balance are more likely to be unstable, and therefore less desirable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the international debt crisis of the 1980s could be avoided by a change in the lending arrangements.
a country that has a stable adjustment path to a shock will have a stable path of debt accumulation.
we have developed a small open economy model that incorporates the effects of international borrowing, the effects of a real depreciation, and the effects of an increase in the trade deficit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a stable adjustment path for a small open country is possible only if the country is able to borrow at a rate linked to its stock of outstanding debt.
a stable adjustment path for the stock of external debt is not a sufficient condition for a stable adjustment path of macroeconomic variables.
the choice of lending arrangement has important implications for the macroeconomic adjustment process.
